name: Colorado
source: Colorado Department of Revenue, Individual Income Tax Guide (revised January 2026, https://tax.colorado.gov/individual-income-tax-guide, read 2026-10-24): flat 4.40% of federal taxable income (rate table to 2025; C.R.S. 39-22-104(1.7)(c) imposes 4.40% from 2022 unless a TABOR temporary cut under 39-22-627 applies, and Legislative Council Staff's TABOR memo of 2026-08-06 expects the next refunds only in tax year 2028); Income Tax Topics: Social Security, Pensions and Annuities (January 2025, read 2026-10-24) for the subtraction; IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 for the federal standard deduction Colorado inherits

state_base.note: Colorado taxes federal taxable income with the additions and subtractions listed in the CDOR Individual Income Tax Guide (revised January 2026, read 2026-10-24): no addition for 401(k)/403(b) deferrals, Traditional IRA deposits or HSA deposits, so they keep their federal treatment (no add-back). Not modelled: the 2026 add-back of the federal overtime deduction (Schedule 1-A; tips need none) and the QBI add-back above 500,000 / 1,000,000 of AGI.

income_brackets.note: Flat 4.40% of federal taxable income: C.R.S. 39-22-104(1.7)(c) and the CDOR Individual Income Tax Guide (revised January 2026, rate table to 2025), read 2026-10-24; Legislative Council Staff's TABOR memo of 2026-08-06 expects no temporary rate cut before tax year 2028.

standard_deduction.note: Colorado taxes federal taxable income (CDOR Individual Income Tax Guide, January 2026), so the federal 2026 standard deduction applies: 16,100 single and separate, 32,200 joint (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.14, read 2026-10-24). Not modelled: the add-back, above 300,000 of AGI, of the standard or itemized deduction over 1,000 single / 2,000 joint from 2026 (12,000 / 16,000 in 2023-2025). The guide lists no add-back of the federal 6,000 senior deduction.

exemptions.note: No Colorado personal or dependent exemptions (CDOR Individual Income Tax Guide, January 2026). senior is the federal additional standard deduction for 65 or older carried in through federal taxable income: 1,650 married, 2,050 unmarried (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.14(3), read 2026-10-24); the married 1,650 is used for single filers too (approximation, 400 low for a single person 65 or older).

retirement_exclusion.note: Pension and annuity subtraction (C.R.S. 39-22-104(4)(f); CDOR Income Tax Topics: Social Security, Pensions and Annuities, January 2025, read 2026-10-24): per person, 20,000 at 55-64 and 24,000 at 65 or older; pensions, annuities, IRA distributions not subject to the early-withdrawal penalty and taxable Social Security share the cap, and one spouse's unused room cannot go to the other. The figures are confirmed primary; the model approximates them as 24,000 per person from 55 (overstates ages 55-64 by 4,000).

estate_inheritance.note: Colorado has no estate tax and no inheritance tax (Tax Foundation 2026 estate and inheritance tax map, https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/estate-inheritance-taxes/, and state-costs.csv columns estate_tax and inheritance_tax agree).

social_security.note: Colorado lets people 65 or older (and 55-64 under 75,000 single / 95,000 joint AGI from 2025) subtract all federally taxed Social Security, but that subtraction uses up the pension subtraction (per person, the larger of the taxed benefits or the 24,000 cap); rules confirmed on the CDOR page in check_at (read 2026-10-24). Approximated as: benefits taxed as on the federal return and retirement income excluded up to 24,000 per person, which is exact while the taxed benefits stay under the cap and the retirement income fills it, and overtaxes benefits above it. The label stays unconfirmed because the treatment is an approximation (owner ruling 2026-10-22).

local_income_tax.note: Colorado's constitution (TABOR) forbids a local income tax (Legislative Council Staff TABOR memo, 2026-08-06). Denver (5.75 a month from employees earning 500 or more a month, Denver Treasury business tax page read 2026-10-24), Aurora, Greenwood Village, Glendale and Sheridan charge flat monthly occupational privilege taxes on wages only, not a rate on income; under 70 a year, so the average rate is 0.

sales_tax.check_at: Colorado revenue department sales and use tax rate tables
sales_tax.source: Tax Foundation, State and Local Sales Tax Rates, Midyear 2026 (https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/2026-sales-tax-rates-midyear/), as of 2026-07-01; groceries and clothing: https://zamp.com/resources/sales-tax-on-groceries and https://zamp.com/blog/sales-tax-on-clothing
sales_tax.note: Rates as fractions; avg_local_rate is the combined less the state rate, at least 0. vehicle_rate is the purchase tax on a car: assumed equal to the combined rate. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py. Groceries and clothing: grocery_rate is the state rate on groceries (0.0) plus the average local rate where locals tax them (locals: partly); research note: State exempt; home-rule cities and some counties tax food; local avg overstates. clothing_taxable is true (research: yes; taxed). Some towns tax groceries and others do not; the estimate uses the general average local rate, so it overstates. Set by hand from .claude/state/research/grocery-tax.csv and clothing-tax.csv (s329).

property_tax.check_at: Census ACS 2024 1-year tables B25090 and B25082 at https://data.census.gov
property_tax.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year (B25090 / B25082) as compiled at https://floridaprobateandfamilylaw.com/blog/effective-property-tax-rates-by-state-2025/
property_tax.note: Effective rate: real-estate taxes paid divided by home value, owner-occupied homes. Senior relief, homestead caps and freezes are not in it (a buyer pays the full rate). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

home_insurance.source: Insurify state table for a 300,000 dwelling (https://insurify.com/homeowners-insurance/states/), October 2026
home_insurance.note: Average annual premium for a 300,000 dwelling. Quote averages differ by 20 to 40 percent between publishers, so the model uses it as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_insurance.source: Insurify full coverage, monthly times 12 (https://insurify.com/car-insurance/states/), October 2026
car_insurance.note: Average annual full-coverage premium. Used as a ratio between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

car_taxes.source: Colorado DMV fact sheet, Motor Vehicle Registration Fees (2018-09-18, read 2026-10-23): flat fees age-of-vehicle 12 (under 7 years), clerk hire 4, county road and bridge 1.50, EMS 2, POST 1, emissions 0.70 + 0.50, insurance 0.50, MIIDB 0.10; FASTER road safety 19.30 and bridge safety 18 for 2,001 to 5,000 lb (secondary: Boulder County fees and taxes page, https://bouldercounty.gov/records/motor-vehicle/additional-motor-vehicle-resources/fees-and-taxes/)
car_taxes.note: Floor: the flat registration fees and FASTER surcharges of a passenger car, 59.60 rounded to 60. The weight-based registration base fee and the specific ownership tax (in place of property tax, high on new cars) are not included, so the real cost is higher. Set by hand (s328, 2026-10-23, owner decision C4: no 0 that only means unknown); a move changes the entered car tax by the dollar difference of the two states' figures, and the importer keeps a non-zero figure.

fuel.note: gas_tax_per_gallon is the state excise in dollars, without sales tax on fuel; average_price_per_gallon is the 2024 average pump price (grade unclear, about regular). Price: 3.06, USGasGauge 2024 nominal average for regular from EIA weekly data (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Gas excise confirmed primary: 22 cents excise plus 6 cents road usage fee for FY 2026-27 (C.R.S. 43-4-217(3)(b)(I)(E)) = 28 cents (validation run 3, 2026-10-22). Set by hand from a secondary source in validation run 3, 2026-10-22; importStateCosts.py keeps a hand-set section.

utilities.source: EIA Electric Power Monthly Table 5.6.B, residential price, January to July 2026
utilities.note: Average residential electricity price in dollars per kWh, January to July 2026 (a partial year). Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

housing.check_at: https://fred.stlouisfed.org (Zillow Home Value Index by state) and https://meric.mo.gov/data/cost-living-data-series
housing.source: Zillow Home Value Index by state via FRED (September 2026); MERIC Cost of Living Data Series housing index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026
housing.note: typical_home_value is the Zillow Home Value Index (all homes, middle tier); cost_index is the MERIC housing cost index (US = 100), used to scale rent after a move. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

health_premiums.check_at: https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/state-indicator/average-marketplace-premiums-by-metal-tier/, Colorado insurance department Medigap rate guide and the CMS MA Landscape and Part D files (https://www.cms.gov)
health_premiums.source: KFF Average Marketplace Premiums by Metal Tier 2026 (benchmark silver at 40, times the federal age curve 2.124 for 60); MoneyGeek Medicare Supplement Plan G at 65, 2026; KFF Average Monthly Premium for PDPs, 2024; MedicareSupplement.com analysis of the CMS 2026 MA Landscape files
health_premiums.note: Monthly premiums per person, unsubsidized list prices: aca_60_monthly is the benchmark silver plan at 60 (estimated from the age-40 figure), medigap_g_monthly Plan G at 65, part_d_monthly the enrollment-weighted Part D plan, medicare_advantage_monthly the average Medicare Advantage premium. Null means no usable figure; a move then leaves that premium unchanged. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

price_indexes.source: MERIC Cost of Living Data Series grocery index (C2ER, US = 100), Q2 2026; BEA Regional Price Parities by state, goods and other services (US = 100), 2024, release of 2026-02-19 via FRED
price_indexes.note: Price levels with US = 100: grocery_index is the MERIC grocery index, bea_goods and bea_services the BEA Regional Price Parities for goods and for services other than rent. Used as ratios between states only. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.

long_term_care.source: Genworth / CareScout Cost of Care Survey 2024, Ranked State Data Tables, state medians (https://assets.carescout.com/a41bb6478c/298701.pdf)
long_term_care.note: State median monthly costs: a home health aide, an assisted living facility and a private nursing home room. Stored for reference; the model does not use them. Imported from .claude/state/research/state-costs.csv and state-costs-2.csv by .claude/state/scratch/importStateCosts.py.
